chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the master of Abyssinia came with the elephant, intending to demolish the Ka'ba, they passed by the camels of Abd al-Muttalib and drove them away. So Abd al-Muttalib directed himself to their leader to ask for the return of his camels. He sought permission to see him, and he granted it. It was said to him: 'This is the noble of Quraysh, or the great one of Quraysh — a man of intellect and noble character.' So he honoured him and drew him near.

Then he said to his interpreter: 'Ask him what his need is.' He said: 'Your companions passed by my camels and drove them away; I would like you to return them to me.' The narrator said: He was astonished at his request to him for the return of the camels, and said: 'This is the one you claim is the great one of Quraysh and whose intellect you praise — and he refrains from asking me to withdraw from the House he worships! But had he asked me to withdraw from demolishing it, I would have done so for him.'

The interpreter informed him of the king's words, and Abd al-Muttalib said to him: 'That House has a Lord who will defend it; I only asked you for my camels because of my need for them.' So he ordered their return to him. Abd al-Muttalib departed until he met the elephant at the edge of the Sanctuary. He called to it: 'Mahmud!' It moved its head. He said to it: 'Do you know why they have brought you?' It shook its head: No. He said: 'They have brought you to demolish the House of your Lord — will you do it?' It shook its head: No.

He (the Imam) said: Abd al-Muttalib departed from it, and they brought the elephant to enter the Sanctuary. When it reached the edge of the Sanctuary, it refused to enter. They struck it but it still refused. They led it around all sides of the Sanctuary — each time it resisted against them and would not enter.

And God sent upon them birds like swallows, each carrying in its beak a stone the size of a lentil or so. Each bird would hover over a man, then release the stone upon his head, and it would come out from his behind — until none remained from them except one man who fled. He went about narrating to people what he had seen, when a bird from among them suddenly appeared. He raised his head and said: 'This is one of those birds.' The bird came and hovered over his head, then cast it upon him; it came out from his behind, and he died.

key_terms.إِنَّ لِذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ رَبًّا يَمْنَعُ: That House has a Lord who will defend it — Abd al-Muttalib's famous declaration of divine protection over the Ka'ba
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ كَالْخَطَاطِيفِ: Birds like swallows — the divinely-sent birds described in Surah al-Fil that destroyed Abraha's army
key_terms.الْفِيلُ: The elephant — the lead war elephant Mahmud, used by Abraha's army; gives the year its name 'Year of the Elephant' (also the title of Surah 105)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةُ: The Ka'ba — the sacred cubic structure in Mecca, the qibla of Muslim prayer
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَبَشَةِ: The master/king of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) — referring to Abraha al-Ashram, the Aksumite viceroy of Yemen who led the Year of the Elephant campaign (~570 CE)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Abraha and the elephant in Al-Kafi hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the story of Abraha, the Abyssinian viceroy who marched with elephants to destroy the Ka'ba. Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather, demonstrated profound trust in God's protection of the Ka'ba — expressing it through his famous statement that the House has a Lord who will defend it. The hadith describes the miracle of Surah al-Fil (Chapter 105), where God destroyed Abraha's army with birds carrying stones, validating the Ka'ba's inviolability in pre-Islamic Arabia.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Humran, and Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the master (king) of Ethiopia came over with the elephants intending to demolish the Kaaba, (he) passed by the camels of Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>, so he took them. 
So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> directed himself<sup>as</sup> to his companions to ask him to return his<sup>as</sup> camels back to him<sup>as</sup>, and he<sup>as</sup> sought permission to see him. So they got the permission for him<sup>as</sup> and said to him, ‘This is a nobleman of Qureysh, or a great one of Qureysh, and he is a man for whom is intellect and a personality. So he honoured him<sup>as</sup> and let him<sup>as</sup> come near.
The he said to his interpretor, ‘Ask him<sup>as</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>as</sup> need?’’ So he<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘Your companions passed by camels of mine, so they took them, therefore I<sup>as</sup> would like you to return these to me<sup>as</sup>’. So he was astounded (surprised) from his<sup>asws</sup> request to him for the return of the camels, and said, ‘This is the one who you all are claiming that he<sup>as</sup> is the great one of Qureysh and mentioned his<sup>as</sup> intellect, neglecting asking me that I should leave from his<sup>as</sup> House (Kaaba) which he<sup>as</sup> worships. But, had he<sup>as</sup> asked me that I should leave from demolishing it, I would have left it for him<sup>as</sup>, from it’. 
So the interpreter informed him<sup>as</sup> of his speech, so Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘For that House (Kaaba) there is a Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Defending it, and rather I<sup>as</sup> asked you to return my camels to me due to my<sup>as</sup> need to these’. So he ordered with their return to him<sup>as</sup> and Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> went away until he<sup>as</sup> came across the elephant upon the side of the Sanctuary. So he<sup>as</sup> said to it: ‘Mahmoud!’ So it moved its head, and he<sup>as</sup> said to it: ‘Do you know for what they have come with you?’ So it said by (shaking) its head, ‘No’. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘They have come with you to demolish the House of your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>. Would you do it?’ So it said by (shaking) its head, ‘No’. 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> left from it and they came over with the elephants in order to enter the Sanctuary. So when they ended up to the side of the Sanctuary, it obstructed from their entering. So they struck it, but it still obstructed. So they circled with it around the Sanctuary, all of it. During each of that it obstructed against them and it did not enter. 
And, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent the birds upon them like swallows. In the beak (of each bird) was a stone like a bean or so. So it hovered on top of the man, then released it upon his head. So it came out from his behind, to the extent that there did not remain anyone from them except for one man who fled. So he went on to narrate to the people with what he saw, when a bird from them emerged, so he raised his head and said, ‘This is the bird from it’, and the bird came over until it hovered on top of his head, then cast it upon him. So it came out from his behind, so he died’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran and Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when the Ethiopian king came with elephants to destroy the Ka‘bah, they passed by the camels of ‘Abd al-Muttalib and took them for themselves. ‘Abd al-Muttalib went to the king, asking him to release his camels. He asked permission for a meeting, which was granted. He (the king) was informed that he (‘Abd al-Muttalib) is the chief honorable man of Quraysh, an intelligent and kind man. The king received him honorably and allowed him to sit very near to the king.

He then said to his translator, ‘Ask him what he needs?’ He (‘Abd al- Muttalib) said, ‘Your people when passing by my camels have taken them away. I like you to return them to me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The king was surprised because of what he had asked, “Return my camels to me.” He said, ‘You think he is the chief of Quraysh and a very intelligent man. He neglects asking me to change my decision about his house of worship. Had he asked me to return back and change my decision I would have done so for his sake/

The translator informed him (‘Abd al- Muttalib) of what the king had said. ‘Abd al-Muttalib said, “This house has an owner who protects it. I ask you to release my camels because I need them.” The king ordered the release of his camels and ‘Abd al-Muttalib returned back. On the way, he saw the elephant on the border of the Sacred area. He said to the elephant, “O Mahmud.” The elephant moved its head in response. He asked, “Do you know why they have brought you?” The elephant with its head said, “No, I do not know.” He said, “They have brought you to destroy the house of your Lord with you. Will you destroy it?” The elephant with its head said, “No, I will not do so.”

He (the Imam) said, ‘’Abd al-Muttalib then left. They brought the elephant to enter the Sacred area, but when on the edge of the Sacred area, it refused to enter/ They tried to force it but it refused to enter. They took the elephant in a circle around the Sacred area. On every point that they tried to force it to enter, it refused to do so and it did not enter.

Allah then sent birds like swallows with stones in their beaks of the size of beans or so, and when on top of the head of a man, they released the stone and it pierced all the way down to come out of his anus. It continued until no one was left from them except one man, who fled and kept telling people about what he had seen. Suddenly one of those birds arrived above him. He raised his head and said, “This is one of them.” The bird came closer over his head and released the stone which pierced down all the way to come out from his anus and he died/”
